title: Publish Settings dialog: wire SWF-output options (compress, omit trace, protect, JPEG quality) into compileDocument
description:
The Publish Settings dialog (File > Publish Settings, Ctrl+Shift+F12) currently only exposes document-level properties (width, height, fps, background colour). The underlying `CompileOptions` interface in `packages/swf/src/compile.ts` already supports `compress`, `protect`, `debugPassword`, `bitmapQuality`, and more — but `usePublish.ts` calls `compileDocument(doc)` with no options, so these switches are permanently off.

## What needs to be done

1. **Extend `PublishSettingsDialog.tsx`** with a 'Flash (.swf)' section containing:
   - Compress movie (zlib/CWS) — checkbox, default off (matches Flash 8 default)
   - Omit trace actions — checkbox (when checked, strip ActionTrace from all DoAction/frame scripts)
   - Protect from import — checkbox (emit Protect tag 24)
   - JPEG quality — 1–100 integer slider/input (passed as `bitmapQuality` to compile)
   - (Optional) Generate size report — checkbox (no-op initially, can log to Output panel later)

2. **Thread settings through to `usePublish`** — `Shell.tsx` already has a `publishSettings` state. Extend it (or add a new `swfPublishOptions` state) to hold the new fields. Pass them into `publishToBytes()` and `testMovie()` as `CompileOptions`.

3. **Implement 'Omit trace actions'** in `compile.ts` if not already there — walk DoAction/ClipAction byte streams and replace ActionTrace (opcode 0x26) calls with no-ops, OR strip them at the AS2 compile step. The simplest path is a flag in `CompileOptions.omitTrace` that the compiler reads when building frame scripts.

4. **Persist settings in the document model** — add an optional `publishOptions` field to `DocumentProperties` (or a top-level `FlashDocument.publishOptions`) so the settings survive Save/Load round-trips. Update FLA serialisation accordingly.

## Files likely touched
- `packages/authoring-ui/src/PublishSettingsDialog.tsx`
- `packages/authoring-ui/src/hooks/usePublish.ts`
- `packages/authoring-ui/src/Shell.tsx`
- `packages/swf/src/compile.ts` (add omitTrace, bitmapQuality plumbing)
- `packages/core/src/model/types.ts` (publishOptions in document model)

## Acceptance criteria
- Enabling 'Compress movie' produces a SWF beginning with `CWS` bytes; disabling it produces `FWS`.
- Enabling 'Protect from import' causes Ruffle to refuse to open the SWF in authoring mode (Protect tag present).
- JPEG quality slider changes the encoded JPEG size of a bitmap-containing SWF.
- Settings survive a Save + Open round-trip.
